query: Which unused models were deleted from bigcachy and l-dev-ai in October 2026, and how much space was reclaimed?

results.document:
# Model cleanup — 2026-10-05

Only downloads excluded from the current hardware registries and Intel runtime were
removed. A model being unloaded was not enough to make it unused: every selectable
profile, draft model, vision projector and split GGUF shard was retained.

| Host | Deleted paths | Allocated bytes reclaimed | Fresh audit |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| bigcachy | 43 | 361,568,317,440 (361.6 GB) | zero further candidates |
| l-dev-ai / Geekom | 24 | 434,316,271,616 (434.3 GB) | zero further candidates |

Both model partitions were verified as XFS. Before deletion, the audit resolved model
symlinks, protected their blobs, checked retained GGUF headers and split-shard counts,
checked Intel exports, and rejected any unrecognized resident model. Dedicated model
cache directories containing a protected file were retained. Recent large downloads
were excluded from automatic deletion.

## Unused model cleanup — 2026-10-05

Verified against every hardware registry entry, all Intel exports and live resident model IDs before deletion. Unloaded alternate profiles are still used and were retained, including draft models, vision projectors and every split shard. Symlink targets were protected as well as model paths; both model filesystems were confirmed XFS.

bigcachy: 43 retired download paths removed, 361,568,317,440 allocated bytes (361.6 GB). l-dev-ai/Geekom: 24 paths, 434,316,271,616 bytes (434.3 GB). Fresh post-cleanup audits on both machines found zero remaining candidates and all retained model files present. Model hosts were serving Radeon/RTX Qwen3.8 and Geekom Flash Next after deletion; other registered profiles remain on disk.

MiniMax, Mistral, Qwen3.6, obsolete Llama vision, stale OpenVINO exports and redundant weight/cache copies were removed. Geekom Q8 and Q4 are pinned to the retained local snapshot so future switching does not fetch another revision. No broad Docker prune, agent-state cleanup or database deletion was performed.

Evidence and the guarded audit script live in lario-llms: docs/MODEL-CLEANUP.md, research/cleanup-summary.json, research/cleanup-bigcachy.json, research/cleanup-geekom.json, corresponding *-after.json audits, and scripts/cleanup_unused_models.py. Always audit again before deleting future downloads; current residency alone does not define use.

MiniMax, Mistral, Qwen3.6, Llama vision, obsolete
OpenVINO exports and redundant model/cache copies. Some retired cache files were
root-owned; only the exact retired directories were removed through Docker. No
general Docker, database or filesystem prune was used.

Full per-path evidence is in `research/cleanup-bigcachy.json` and
`research/cleanup-geekom.json`; fresh audits are the corresponding `*-after.json`
files. `research/cleanup-summary.json` records totals. These are allocated file
bytes, not an assertion that filesystem free space will increase by exactly that
amount under concurrent activity.

Re-audit on the model's owner using:

```sh
python3 scripts/cleanup_unused_models.py --output /tmp/model-cleanup-plan.json
```

Review the plan before adding `--apply`. The script aborts if retained weights or
the XFS mount are missing, or a live model is outside the registry. The inventory
is scoped to dedicated model download locations; project files, datasets, agent
state and databases are outside its deletion scope.

## Other cleanup on bigcachy

- `~/Projects/timbuk2` (1.3 GB, three `t2-mono` clones) — deleted
- SSH key `id_ed25519_bigcachy_timbuk2_github` and its `~/.ssh/config` `Host github.com-timbuk2` block — deleted
- `~/.gitconfig-timbuk2` — deleted
- `~/.gitconfig`: the `includeIf "gitdir:~/Projects/timbuk2/"` entry and the `url.insteadOf` rewrite for `bantubyte` — removed
- `~/.config/gh-timbuk2` — removed; associated GitHub token revoked
- `gh-timbuk2()` shell function — removed from `~/.zshrc`
- `~/db backups/` (note the space, not a slash) — 4.6 GB of 2026-05-29 seed dumps: `multi-tenant.sql` (2.1 GB), `primedia.sql` (2.0 GB), `pikaboo.sql` (590 MB) — deleted
- `~/pikadata/`, `~/.pgverify/`, `~/hermes-db-backup-20260731T013255/` — deleted



## Related: nanoclaw removal

The `nanoclaw/` directory and `deploy/deploy-nanoclaw.sh` were already removed from the agents repo earlier, in commit `d076ef3` (`fleet: remove the Nanoclaw runtime`). Nothing named nanoclaw exists anywhere under `/home/lario` today.

What this decommission removed was the leftover *documentation* — stale prose in `initial-prompt.md` and across this knowledge base that still described nanoclaw as a live agent type. The t2-coder-1/2/3 agents named there were Nanoclaw-based Timbuk2 coding agents that never ran; their intended workspaces were the three `~/Projects/timbuk2/t2-mono-{1,2,3}` clones deleted here.
